binary: manhunt.exe (2004 retail build, PE32/i386, no ASLR, ImageBase 0x00400000)
summary: Fully drivable unattended, character movement included (since 2026-09-11). Self-launch works but stops at an ANSI Win32 launcher dialog that must be BM_CLICKed. The MOUSE is read through DirectInput, and proxy-side synthetic DIMOUSESTATE2 drives the cursor, menu highlight, menu clicks and the in-game camera. The KEYBOARD is read from ordinary window messages: PostMessage(WM_KEYDOWN / WM_KEYUP) straight to the game window walks, strafes and runs the character with the default bindings (W/A/S/D, Shift to run, Enter/Space to use). SendInput returns success but never reaches the game -- do not use it. IMPORTANT: two harness defects made this game look completely input-proof until 2026-09-10 and every input finding before that date is withdrawn -- see input.harness_traps.

measured_paths.claim: The game polls the DirectInput MOUSE ~64,000 times a second in the menu and ~200 a second (the frame rate) in gameplay, with cbData = 20 (DIMOUSESTATE2). It calls GetDeviceState on the KEYBOARD about once a frame with cbData = 0 -- on purpose: that single call site (0x00492376) is a 'still acquired?' probe with a re-Acquire loop, and the game never reads key state through DirectInput at all. GetDeviceData is never called on either device.
measured_paths.how: per-device counters in the project's own d3d8 proxy (input.c REPORT command); call site from static analysis of the unpacked image (verified-numerically 2026-09-11)
measured_paths.implication: Mouse: inject into GetDeviceState on the MOUSE device. Keyboard: post window messages. Injecting DIK state through the proxy can never press a key in this game.
measured_paths.supersedes: the 2026-09-10 claim that the keyboard count 'freezes once gameplay starts' -- it pauses during the level load and resumes in play

working.route: Proxy-side synthetic DIMOUSESTATE2 (relative deltas + buttons) added into the buffer returned by GetDeviceState on the SysMouse device, driven by the manhunt_vr_input.txt script file
working.result: main menu -> SELECT SCENE -> BORN AGAIN -> live gameplay, entirely unattended; camera pans ~90 degrees on one move in gameplay
working.how_to_get_it_right: Movement axes are RELATIVE and the game polls ~20,000x/sec, so a delta added on every poll is 100x the intended motion. Hand movement over in TICKS at a real-mouse report rate (~8 ms / 125 Hz), spread over a requested duration. Buttons are the opposite -- a LEVEL, ORed on every poll, because a button missed for one frame is a dropped click.

calibration_dev_pc.note: Measured from a controlled 100-count move away from both window edges. The engine's known horizontal stretch is 1.39x (a 1.28 aspect rendered into a 1.7778 backbuffer), which is suggestively close but not proven to be the same number.
calibration_dev_pc.warning: Moves that reach a window edge CLAMP silently and make the rate look like 0.70 px/count. Calibrate away from the edges.

working.route: A synthetic left click during the intro credits
working.result: main menu reached 16-28 s after the click instead of the ~180 s the credits take on their own

working.route: PostMessage(hwnd, WM_KEYDOWN, vk, lParam) then later WM_KEYUP, posted straight to the game's main window from an external 64-bit PowerShell
drives: walk back (S), strafe left (A), strafe right (D)
run (Shift vk 0x10 held together with W)
working.result: the character walks, strafes and runs; one key-down with no auto-repeat is enough for a held action
working.how_to_get_it_right: lParam = 1 | (scancode << 16) | (extended << 24); WM_KEYUP adds bits 30 and 31. Arrow keys NEED the extended bit (24) or the game reads them as the numpad keys. Foreground the window first; the main loop only runs a frame while the window has focus.
working.bindings_default: Forward Up/W, Back Down/S, Strafe Left/A, Right/D, Run Right Ctrl/Shift, Sneak Numpad 0/Left Ctrl (plain Ctrl is SNEAK), Use Enter/Space, Attack Left mouse, Action 2 Middle mouse, Reload Numpad 1/R, Inventory swap Right mouse/Tab, Look back Numpad 4/F, Peek Delete/Page Down or Q/E, First person End/X, Pause Esc, Items 1-4, Inventory up/down wheel. Read from the binary's default tables; Documents\Manhunt User Files\SaveGames\Settings.dat was byte-identical to them (verified-numerically 2026-09-11).

disproved.route: Proxy-side synthetic DirectInput KEYBOARD state, with the keyboard device's vtable genuinely hooked
disproved.result: no effect; cursor did not move and the highlight did not change. The keyboard device is called with cbData = 0 and never returns key state.
disproved.explained: 2026-09-11: the game never reads keys through DirectInput (its one keyboard GetDeviceState is an acquisition probe with cbData = 0). This route can never work, on any screen.

disproved.route: SendInput scancodes W (0x11) and Up arrow (0x48 + KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY), 40-byte INPUT, return value confirmed as 1 down / 1 up
disproved.result: scene unchanged; the character did not move -- including on 2026-09-11 straight after a POSTED W had walked him, in the same spot
disproved.scope_warning: The keys are right (W and extended Up are FORWARD). The failure is delivery: SendInput reports success but the key never reaches the game's window procedure. Why is open -- injected input going to a different keyboard-focus thread, or a filter on this machine, are both hypotheses. Use PostMessage instead.

disproved.route: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-10: all SendInput results recorded before 2026-09-10b (keyboard scancodes, absolute mouse move + click, relative mouse move)
disproved.result: Not evidence. SendInput was returning 0 with GetLastError = 87 and inserting zero events -- see input.harness_traps. These were never tests.

disproved.route: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-10: 'the white arrow beside the menu entries is menu art and never moves'
disproved.result: It is the CURSOR. It moves exactly as one under synthetic DIMOUSESTATE2, and the menu highlight follows whichever entry it is over. It never moved before because nothing was ever delivered to the mouse.

harness_traps.trap: Only the FIRST DirectInput device was hooked
harness_traps.detail: The proxy guarded its vtable hooks with a single global flag. This game creates SysMouse first and SysKeyboard second, and the two devices do NOT share a vtable (mouse 0x742395F4, keyboard 0x74239570, different real function pointers). The keyboard was therefore never instrumented, and the recorded 'GetDeviceState = 11,917,105 on the mouse, 0 on the keyboard' was an uninstrumented device reporting nothing -- not a measurement. Synthetic keyboard state was likewise never installed in the keyboard's vtable, so 'the keyboard route does not work' was untested.
harness_traps.fix: Hook every distinct vtable, keep the original function pointers PER vtable, and publish each record before patching its slots.

harness_traps.trap: SendInput never sent anything (this one is universal, not Manhunt-specific)
harness_traps.detail: The PowerShell harness declared the INPUT struct as 28 bytes -- the 32-bit layout -- while running in 64-bit PowerShell, where INPUT is 40 bytes (DWORD type, 4 bytes of padding, then a 32-byte union). Every call returned 0 with GetLastError = 87 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) and inserted ZERO events. Nothing checked the return value, so it read as 'the game ignores synthetic input'.
harness_traps.fix: Always assert SendInput's return value equals the number of events passed, and log GetLastError when it does not. A silently failing input API and an ignored input API are indistinguishable from outside.

untried: SendInput from INSIDE the 32-bit game process (the project's kbdprobe.c 'KI' command, compiled but not wired) -- would separate 'injected input is filtered' from 'it goes to the wrong focus thread'.
A gamepad, via the game's GAME_CONTROL_TYPE setting -- never tried.

entry_points.name: steam-launch
entry_points.notes: Reaches the launcher dialog in roughly 20-25 s. The proxy DLL loads and patches within 0.6 s of process start.

entry_points.name: launcher-dialog
entry_points.how: A top-level window titled MANHUNT owns a small dialog ('Manhunt launcher', ~414x346) with Play / Quit buttons and video settings. Enumerate its child windows and send BM_CLICK (0x00F5) to the child whose text is 'Play'.
entry_points.hazard: Read child window text with GetWindowTextA, NOT GetWindowTextW. The dialog is ANSI, so the W variant returns only the first character - 'P' for Play, 'Q' for Quit - which reads exactly like 'no Play button found'. Same for GetClassNameA ('B' instead of 'BUTTON').

entry_points.name: skip-the-frontend
entry_points.how: Edit initscripts/FRONTEND/settings.txt with the game CLOSED: set SKIP_MENU 1 and START_LEVEL 0 (the built-in 'Test level'). Launch, click Play in the launcher dialog, then wait ~50 s.
entry_points.result: lands directly in live 3D - real in-engine rendering with HUD, crosshair and subtitles - with no frontend involved. Ran 3 min 30 s before hitting a separate, understood crash (spline table, see hazards).
entry_points.notes: DOES NOT REACH GAMEPLAY on the stock game: the level's folder name is copied before levels.txt is read, so the world never loads, the load retries every frame and memory runs out (crash at 0x0061166A, or 0x00496C4F with the project's TOC fix). The level's intro Bink movie still plays, which looks like success. The 2026-09-10 'lands in live 3D' was very probably the reporter's camcorder movie. With the project's opt-in level-name fix (flag file manhunt_vr_fix_levelname) there is no crash but the screen stays black (2026-09-11). START_LEVEL is a raw index into initscripts/LEVELS/levels.txt: 0 = Jury_Turf (BORN AGAIN), 1 = Derelict; the '0 : Test level' comment in settings.txt is stale. Use the menu. Set SKIP_MENU back to 0 afterwards.

routes.how: BM_CLICK (0x00F5) the child button whose GetWindowTextA is 'Play'
a synthetic left click (MB 0) -- reached the menu 16-28 s later instead of the ~180 s the credits take on their own

Move the cursor onto SELECT SCENE with synthetic mouse deltas, CAPTURE and VERIFY the highlight, left-click; then move onto the first scene thumbnail, verify again, click. Reaches live gameplay in about a minute.
routes.calibration_note: From the post-click cursor spot beside PLAY, M 45 -37 lands on PLAY and M 72 -10 on SELECT SCENE; on the scene grid, M -168 -107 lands on BORN AGAIN (dev PC, 800x600 client). PLAY always starts level 0 (BORN AGAIN), whatever START_LEVEL says.
routes.supersedes: the 2026-09-10 entry that recorded this route as UNSOLVED
routes.hazard: QUIT is the bottom entry of the main menu. Never blind key-count or blind-move past it -- move, capture, verify the highlight, and only then click.

routes.how: synthetic mouse X deltas; ~900 counts pans roughly 90 degrees

The project's proxy (build 8ceea3a4+) has a POS script command that logs the player's map position (X, Y, Z-up) and yaw (0 = +X, 90 = +Y, counter-clockwise) read from memory: player [0x00715B9C], frame [[player+0x80]+4], position frame+0x40, forward frame+0x30 (engine Y-up; map = (x, -z, y)). Loop: POS -> turn the camera by -(bearing - yaw) / 0.343 synthetic mouse-X counts -> post W for distance / 2.2 seconds -> repeat. Straight lines hit walls; use waypoints.
routes.calibration: +100 synthetic mouse-X counts = yaw -34.3 deg (positive X turns clockwise); walking ~2.2 map units/s; item pickup radius ~0.5

routes.how: The project's proxy HUNTERS command logs each hunter's map position, facing, health, state and whether the player is BEHIND him. Sneak (hold Left Ctrl: WM_KEYDOWN vk 0x11 scan 0x1D, not extended, together with W) toward him turning at most ~25 deg per step, re-reading HUNTERS each step; at ~1.1 m while BEHIND, hold the attack button (synthetic left mouse) ~1.5 s. The green lock-on triangles appear first; the camcorder execution scene follows; HUNTERS then reads health -1, state 0x1B DEAD.
routes.warning: Walking in from the front turns it into a fist fight (state 0xF) that the player tends to lose. A weapon must be in hand; the plastic bag is used up by one execution.

routes.from: in-game, standing on a second item
routes.how: Hold the INVENTORY SWAP key (Tab, vk 0x09 scan 0x0F, or right mouse) ~1.5 s when the game shows 'Press and hold the inventory button to swap this item'.

PLAY shows a BRIGHTNESS screen (Enter = OK; a mouse click on OK did not register), then DIFFICULTY (FETISH highlighted = standard; Enter), then a SAVE GAME slot list (Enter saves to the highlighted slot; Esc continues without saving), then 'Game saved successfully' (Enter). ⚠️ With any save present, PLAY instead CONTINUES the newest save by its internal timestamp — it is not a fresh start.
Enter = Continue (restart from the last checkpoint); Esc = quit to menu.
Posted WM_KEYDOWN Enter (vk 0x0D, scan 0x1C) confirms (loaded a save); Esc (vk 0x1B, scan 0x01) backs out. The mouse route also works.
PostMessage WM_KEYDOWN / WM_KEYUP to the game window: W forward, S back, A / D strafe, Shift + W run (see input.working)

settings_file.notes: Plain text, read at startup only - edit with the game closed. Useful keys: START_LEVEL (0 = Test level, 1-n = real levels), SKIP_MENU (1 = boot straight into START_LEVEL), GAME_CONTROL_TYPE, GAME_CONTROL_INVERT_Y, FX_MODE. There is also a 'Frontend disable (FOR DEBUG ONLY!)' option.

registry.notes: Device / Mode / Index. Mode is a RenderWare video-mode index handed verbatim to RwEngineSetVideoMode. Deleting the Video key makes the game recreate its defaults. On the dev PC, mode index 0 enumerated as 1920x1080 WINDOWED (the desktop resolution).

capture.method: BitBlt from the screen DC (Graphics.CopyFromScreen over the window rect), after SetForegroundWindow
capture.warning: Do not use PrintWindow - it serves stale DWM-cached frames when the game stops presenting, with no error. This is a portfolio-wide rule, not specific to Manhunt.
capture.notes: The game window is a normal top-level window; the proxy resizes its client area to 800x600. Several invisible top-level windows share the PID, so pick the largest VISIBLE one.

hazards.what: Spline table overflow crash -- RELOCATED, and it held for one level
hazards.detail: The spline (camera path) loader wrote into a fixed 100-entry table at 0x007134F4 whose count sits in the word immediately after the last slot (0x00713684), with no bounds check; the 101st spline overwrote the count and the next iteration faulted at 0x00471FFB. Clamping the count (SPLINEGUARD) removed that crash but only MOVED the fault to a memcpy into a null spline at 0x0061166A. The project's proxy now RELOCATES the table to a 1024-slot buffer (SPLINERELOC) after verifying that the base literal occurs exactly six times in the whole image and that nothing reaches the table by a computed base. A full real level then ran ~8 minutes with no overflow and no crash. 2026-09-11: a SKIP_MENU direct start with the relocation logged no overflow and no 0x00471FFB -- but still crashed at 0x0061166A, identically to the earlier runs, so that second crash is NOT caused by dropped splines. It happens only on the direct start; the same level through the menu ran most of an hour.

Sixteen call sites in the retail exe run leftover anti-tamper checks that deliberately sabotage the game (stuck gates, item/useable crashes, broken saving, ammo drain). The project's proxy patches all sixteen at runtime, first try on every launch that carried them. Confirmed firing IN GAMEPLAY for the first time on 2026-09-10: Broken Health 1, Broken SaveGame EntityData, and Help Text Crash (the last roughly every 5-8 s), all returning the repaired value with the game continuing normally. 2026-09-11: those three again, plus Broken Level Initialization 1 and Ignore Control 1 for the first time (a timer: 10 minutes apart); the player still had full control 24-34 minutes after Ignore Control fired. Without the proxy, expect the documented bug cluster.

hazards.what: The game pauses itself when its window loses focus
hazards.detail: The pause menu (SETTINGS / QUIT / CONTINUE) opens whenever another window takes focus -- including a person typing into another app on the same PC. Synthetic input then moves the menu cursor and nothing in the world changes, which reads exactly like 'stuck'. Esc does not close this menu; Enter on the highlighted CONTINUE does. ⚠️ QUIT is directly above CONTINUE: verify the highlight before pressing Enter.

hazards.what: Restart / save-load crash from the project's own SecuROM site-1 patch (FIXED, opt-in)
hazards.detail: The project's patch for 'Broken SaveGame EntityData' wrote 1 where the game writes 0, which made the entity snapshot record one entity 12 bytes short; every restart after death and every load of a save written by those builds crashed at 0x00431820 ('No archetype of this name exists : d'). Fixed in the project's proxy by manhunt_vr_fix_entitydata (write stock, repair poisoned snapshots on re-parse), all live checks passed 2026-09-11. Poisoned saves can also be repaired offline (one byte).

The exe is packed at rest by a SecuROM protector stub and external debugger attach fails ('Could not open process'). All static analysis must be done against a dump of the unpacked image; all patching must be done in-process from an injected DLL.

hazards.what: Window-edge clamping makes mouse calibration lie
hazards.detail: A synthetic mouse move that reaches a window edge stops there silently. Two probe moves that both clamped made the cursor rate look like 0.70 px/count when it is 1.87 (X) and 1.36 (Y). Calibrate with a move that starts and ends well away from every edge.

process_exit.how: SendMessage(hwnd, WM_CLOSE) to the game's visible top-level window
process_exit.notes: Exits cleanly, no taskkill needed. Historically, once the SecuROM bug cluster has been hit in gameplay the process can become unresponsive and need a force-kill; that has not recurred since the DRM patches went in, but n is small.
